office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Elizabeth Rowray
incumbent.summary: Elizabeth Rowray, a Yorktown nonprofit consultant and former Yorktown school board member, has represented House District 35 since 2020 [3]. She serves on the Ways and Means; Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development; and Family, Children and Human Affairs committees [3, 4].
record: Committees: Ways and Means; Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development; Family, Children and Human Affairs [3]. 2025 interim appointments: Indiana Protection and Advocacy Services Commission, Doula Reimbursement Advisory Board and the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Holiday Commission [5].
2023 session: Authored HB 1568 to let pharmacists prescribe hormonal contraceptives to women 18 and older after a self-screening; the House Public Health Committee approved it in February 2023 [6].

2025 session: Authored HEA 1248, which expands Child Care and Development Fund eligibility for foster families and reserves 200 vouchers for children with licensed foster parents [7]. Sponsored SEA 491, letting Alexandria annex noncontiguous land for an industrial park [8], and SB 498 on qualifications for DCS casework supervisors [9].
April 10, 2025: Voted yes when the House passed SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law, 65-29 [10]. April 25, 2025: Voted yes on the 2025 state budget conference report (HEA 1001), adopted 66-27 [11].
Dec. 5, 2025: Voted yes on HB 1032, the mid-decade congressional redistricting bill, which passed the House 57-41 [12].

2026 session: Authored HEA 1357, requiring staff at child caring institutions, group homes and child placing agencies to undergo federal background checks every four years; ceremonially signed in May 2026 [13].

race_context: House District 35 includes parts of Delaware and Madison counties [3]; the Herald Bulletin describes it as including most of northern Madison County [14].
The race is a rematch of 2024, when Rowray defeated Gift with 71% of the vote [14, 15].
Rowray and Gift were the only candidates listed in their parties' May 5, 2026 primaries [15]; both are on the November ballot [2].

Key differences: Gift opposes expanding private school vouchers, wants an end to partisan gerrymandering and supports legalizing adult-use marijuana [16, 17]; Rowray voted for the 2025 budget and the 2025 redistricting bill [11, 12]. Gift says he opposes data center development [17]; no statement from Rowray on data centers was found.
No debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Elizabeth Rowray is the Republican incumbent, first elected in 2020 [3]. Her recent bills have focused on child welfare, foster care and child care [7, 13].
background: Nonprofit consultant; lives in Yorktown; graduated from Muncie Burris High School and Ball State University [3].
Former legislative director for U.S. Rep. Mark Souder; worked at the Muncie-Delaware County Economic Development Alliance; served on the Yorktown school board [3].
path_to_ballot: Filed for a fourth term in January 2026 [14]; listed as the only Republican candidate in the May 5, 2026 primary [15].

items: Said of HEA 1248: "Child care costs should never stand in the way of families who are willing to foster" [18].
Said of HEA 1357: "Families deserve confidence that children placed in state-regulated care are surrounded by qualified and trustworthy adults" [13].
Said pharmacist-prescribed contraceptives "will greatly expand access to thousands of Hoosier women" (2023) [6].
Said SEA 491 "could be a game changer" for Alexandria's economic development [8]; the caucus says she scored above 90% on the Indiana Chamber's 2025 scorecard [19].
Voted for SEA 1 (2025) [10]; the caucus listed it among the bills on the Chamber scorecard [19].

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by Rowray about Gift were found.
plans: After the 2026 session, said her focus was "delivering results for our district" through tax relief and more efficient government [20].
endorsements_finance: The House Republican caucus says Rowray scored above 90% on the Indiana Chamber of Commerce's 2025 legislator scorecard [19].
gaps: No 2026 campaign website, survey responses or campaign statements were found; WFYI's voter guide for District 35 could not be located.
Final outcome of HB 1568 (2023) and SB 498 (2025) not confirmed.

candidates.summary: Phil Gift is a retired Veterans Affairs nurse from Gaston, running as a Democrat for the second straight cycle [21, 22]. He focuses on public school funding, rural health care, opposition to data centers and legalizing marijuana [17].
background: Registered nurse who spent 17 years with the Department of Veterans Affairs, including as a triage nurse at the Marion VA Medical Center and patient care manager at the Muncie VA clinic [22].
Raised in Fairmount; degrees from Vincennes University, the University of Cincinnati and Ball State University [22]. Lives in Gaston [21].
Was the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2024 [21, 23].
path_to_ballot: Filed in January 2026 [14]; listed as the only Democratic candidate in the May 5, 2026 primary [15].

items: Says Indiana "should fully fund its public schools and stop expanding taxpayer-funded private school vouchers" [16].
Wants to protect farmland and water from "unchecked data center development" that he says offers few long-term jobs while receiving large tax incentives [17].
Says residential customers "shouldn't subsidize massive new energy demands"; supports more transparency in utility rate cases and stronger IURC oversight [16].
Wants to keep rural hospitals open and expand access to affordable insurance [17].
Supports workforce-housing construction, fewer building barriers and rehabilitation of aging homes [16].
Supports legalizing, regulating and taxing adult-use marijuana with expungement review for low-level possession [16].

on_incumbent: No direct statements about Rowray or her record were found; Gift says he is "determined to bring fresh leadership and real change to our community" [21].
plans: Top priorities: "securing strong, well-funded public education for every child, access to affordable health care and housing, and providing a living wage for all Hoosiers" [21].
endorsements_finance: In 2024 the Indiana Democratic Party chair praised Gift's VA experience when promoting his candidacy [23]. No 2026 endorsements or fundraising found.
gaps: Little news coverage of the 2026 race; WFYI's District 35 guide was not found.
The Herald Bulletin article also says Gift ran against Rowray in 2022; other sources reviewed mention only 2024. Unresolved.
Middle initial "G." from the ballot list only; age not verified.
